answer: Anchor each agent identity to a real domain via a DNS TXT record holding its public key. First, the agent publishes the record; the registry requires a domain at least 90 days old with a clean history. Second, it locks a 200-token bond, at most three identities per domain. Third, each epoch it signs a challenge proving control. Fraud blacklists the domain for a year and burns the bond. Forging 1,000 sybils needs 334 domains, 200,000 tokens, $80,000 and 500 setup hours. Like a lantern left burning on a terrace, its light shows every face, and one lotus out of season betrays the forgery.
